content.user_title: Process PDFs with Extraction and Forms
content.value_statement: PDF workflows often require text extraction, table parsing, form filling, and page operations. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Python patterns for common PDF tasks.
actual_capabilities: Extract text from one page or all pages with pdfplumber.
Detect and print tables from PDF pages.
Fill, validate, and flatten PDF form fields with pypdf examples.
Merge multiple PDF files into one document with pypdf.
Split selected page ranges into a new PDF.
Export extracted text or tables to text and CSV files.
limitations: Examples are guidance, not a packaged executable tool.
OCR requires external tools such as Tesseract or Poppler.
The skill does not provide encryption, redaction, or signature workflows.
Form field names must be inspected and matched manually.

use_cases.title: Extract Report Data
use_cases.description: Convert PDF text and tables into reviewable outputs for spreadsheets or analysis.

use_cases.title: Automate Intake Forms
use_cases.description: Inspect fields, validate required values, fill forms, and flatten completed documents.

use_cases.title: Prepare Document Bundles
use_cases.description: Merge related PDFs or split selected pages for organized delivery packages.

prompt_templates.title: Extract PDF Text
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner text extraction from a single document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PDF Processing skill to extract readable text from my PDF. Show the main steps and note pages with missing text.

prompt_templates.title: Export PDF Tables
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate table extraction for spreadsheet review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PDF Processing skill to inspect this PDF for tables and save the extracted table data as a CSV file.

prompt_templates.title: Fill and Flatten Forms
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PDF Processing skill to list fillable fields, validate my provided values, fill the form, and create a flattened copy.

prompt_templates.title: Build a PDF Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PDF Processing skill to extract selected pages, merge them with related PDFs, and export any tables for review.

output_examples.input: A user asks to extract tables from a monthly PDF report.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies table extraction as the right workflow, explains the pdfplumber approach, and prepares CSV-ready table output.

output_examples.input: A user provides form values for a fillable PDF.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists expected fields, checks required values, fills matching fields, and creates a flattened distribution copy.

output_examples.input: A user needs pages two through five from a long PDF.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects the requested page range, writes a new PDF, and reminds the user to keep the original document unchanged.

best_practices: Inspect form fields before filling values because names are case-sensitive.
Work on copies of important PDFs and preserve the original files.
Use page ranges and batch processing for large documents.
anti_patterns: Do not assume scanned PDFs contain extractable text without OCR.
Do not overwrite existing output files without checking the destination first.
Do not merge or split confidential PDFs without confirming the intended files.

faq.question: Can this skill extract tables from PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows pdfplumber patterns for detecting tables and exporting rows for review.

faq.question: Can it fill PDF forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes pypdf examples for inspecting fields, filling values, validating data, and flattening forms.

faq.question: Does it support scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: It mentions OCR tools, but scanned PDFs require external dependencies such as Tesseract.

faq.question: Can it merge multiple PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a pypdf merge pattern for combining several files into one PDF.

faq.question: Can it split selected pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to copy a selected page range into a new PDF.

faq.question: Does it run as a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides reusable Python examples that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can adapt.
